findings.text: 30 chemotype(s); the largest holds 60 of 147 molecules -- a series of several scaffolds has no common frame, and an alignment will invent one
the common framework (framework of the largest chemotype) has 18 heavy atoms, about 82% of a typical molecule, and 42% of the set can be cut at it
the 18 shared framework atoms sit 0.1 A apart between molecules, over the best of their matches (62 of 147 carry them)
the aligned model is +0.085 in q2 against counts (95% interval -0.099 to +0.281) -- the frame gains nothing over counts
the aligned model is -0.126 in q2 against invariant (95% interval -0.324 to +0.050) -- the frame gains nothing over invariant
the aligned model is +0.069 in q2 against topomer (95% interval -0.111 to +0.276) -- cutting the molecules and posing the pieces by rule does as well as the frame, on the molecules that can be cut
the aligned model is +0.147 in q2 against descriptors (95% interval -0.026 to +0.315) -- descriptors alone do as well, so the geometry adds nothing on this set

why: the frame gains nothing over invariant, which needs no alignment to curate and cannot be done wrongly
